messages:
Arun: Nightdash fired at 23:53 UTC — p95 latency +120ms and KV cache hitrate fell ~18% right after the midnight rollout. Graphs: https://dash/reds/nightdash/alerts/1766347890

Maggie: I see it. Correlates with the kernel-selector changes from PR #6421 (rolled at 23:50). Selector started preferring the 'stream-optimized' kernel for short sequences which is strange for these workloads.

Jules: Can we bisect to that PR quickly? Perf-bot flagged a regression in the nightly run: p95 +120ms, throughput -9% (00:00-01:00).

perf-bot: nightly-regression: metric=p95_latency delta=+120ms window=1h trace=trace-0a1b2c

Arun: I sampled a few traces and ran a quick flameprof on a failing request. Snippet:
```
CPU total: 78ms -> 152ms
kernel_select: 34ms
kv_lookup: 18ms
kv_miss_path: 60ms
serialize_after_kernel: 22ms
```

Maggie: Looking at kernel-selector logs from the canary hosts, there is kernel churn per request. Excerpt:
```
[23:52:59] select_kernel(req=abc, seq=64) -> stream_opt (score 0.62)
[23:52:59] select_kernel(req=abc, seq=64) -> dense_opt (fallback, score 0.61)
[23:53:00] exec using dense_opt -> warmup path hit -> KV lookup invalidation
```

Jules: That explains the CPU redo + KV TTL churn — switching kernels invalidates some prefetched execution state and causes extra KV misses. If churn oscillates across short windows, hitrate tanked.

Arun: Reproduced locally with a replay of the failing traffic pattern (short sequences + interleaved long ones). Kernel scores hover around the decision boundary and small quantization in the scoring function flips selection.

Maggie: Quick mitigation: revert PR #6421 to confirm. If revert restores baseline, we know kernel selector change is the culprit.

deploy-bot: rollback requested for rollout/2026-03-17-23:50 -> queued for canary.

Arun: Opening revert CL now and kicking off a canary. CI artifacts: https://ci/reports/6421-revert.

ci-runner: canary run started (2 hosts). Perf artifacts: https://ci/artifacts/1766347890/canary

perf-bot: Canary results: p95 within +5ms of baseline on canary hosts after revert; KV hitrate back to baseline. Full rollback recommended.

Jules: Agreed — roll back rollout/2026-03-17-23:50. Also follow-up work: make kernel-selector decisions sticky for N requests to avoid oscillation and add a regression test with mixed-seq traffic.

Maggie: I'll create a design doc for sticky-kernel policy and a unit test harness for selector stability under jitter. Also propose adding a small hysteresis to the scoring to avoid flipping for marginal deltas.

Arun: Created issue RG-1203 with repro steps, links, and assign: Maggie + Jules. Revert CL merged and rollout completed. Will monitor next nightly. :thumbsup:

Jules: Postmortem note: include the selector scoring precision/quantization as root cause and the rollback timeline in release notes.

Arun: Thanks team — keeping this thread live with overnight metrics.
